changeSet.author: dev
changeSet.comment:
Every order creation numbers the order with MAX(user_order_number) + 1 for its user, and does so while holding that user's balance row lock — so a reseller's concurrent orders queue behind this query one at a time. Without an index it read every one of the user's orders across all partitions (prod, reseller User#856: ~57k rows, ~44 ms per order, growing with every order). With (user_id, user_order_number) PostgreSQL answers it with one backward index-only probe per partition (~1 ms). The user's /orders list, which sorts by user_order_number, benefits too.
orders is partitioned by created_at: an index on the parent is created on every existing partition and automatically on every future one (PartitionMaintenanceScheduler). CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY is not supported on a partitioned parent; a plain build takes a SHARE lock on each partition only for the build (~0.1 s for ~60k rows), and Liquibase runs at application startup, before the panel accepts orders.
changeSet.sql: CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_orders_user_order_number ON orders (user_id, user_order_number);
